decisions.reason: This definition fixes finite-sum, square-root, maximum and counting-inner-product conventions and correctly proves their well-definedness. It need not duplicate the separate proved Euclidean triangle inequality: lem-nufft-finite-euclidean-norm-triangle, steps 1.1 and 2.1, obtains Cauchy-Schwarz from the nonnegative projection residual and then the squared-norm inequality. Positivity and definiteness follow from nonnegative moduli and a positive nonzero coordinate; homogeneity follows from modulus multiplicativity (and uniqueness of the nonnegative square root for l2). The l1 triangle inequality follows by summing scalar triangle inequalities; the maximum version follows by bounding each coordinate. The empty array is the sole vector of C^empty and has norm zero. No circular premise or choice principle is needed.

The actual declared dependency def-nufft-periodized-gaussian-gridding-kernel defines phi_tau(t)=sum_n exp(-pi(t+n)^2/tau). With y=Mx and m=ell+nM, pi(ell/M-x+n)^2/tau=pi(m-y)^2/(tau M^2), exactly the exponent a=pi/(tau M^2). Euclidean division makes this reindexing bijective, and the proved absolute convergence licenses it. Half-open distance shells contain at most two integers, giving S. Omitted residues lift into the full lattice tail |m-y|>w; bounding this superset on each side by its first term plus the decreasing Gaussian integral gives exp(-aw^2)(1+1/(2aw)). The integral bound follows by comparison with t/w and FTC applied to -exp(-at^2)/(2a); its integrand is continuous and w>=1. Nonnegative finite product sums and the union bound give T_d. The included cutoff endpoints, dimension one, positive denominators and no-choice claim are sound. The judges missing supplied interface does not establish a defect in the item.
